subject: Re: VP Clinical Ops — finalist decision
snippet: Team, I've had a chance to sit with everything Rich sent over, and I want to walk through my thinking before Marcus and Rich move on the offer, because I know this isn't the direct
body_text:
Team,

I've had a chance to sit with everything Rich sent over, and I want to walk through my thinking before Marcus and Rich move on the offer, because I know this isn't the direction most of us were leaning two weeks ago.

When we first got the slate, I was genuinely torn — Dr. Castellano's clinical background is a better direct match for what Priscilla's team needs day to day, and Doug's read on her interview was strong. I said as much on the 29th, and I meant it. If the reference checks had come back clean, I think we'd be sending her an offer today.

But they didn't come back clean, and I don't think we can talk ourselves past what two independent references told Rich separately: three departures from her direct reports in eighteen months, both references describing it as connected to how she managed performance conversations rather than normal attrition. That's not a single data point I'm willing to write off as noise, especially walking into a department that's already short-staffed and where Priscilla and her charge nurses are stretched thin as it is. If we bring in a leader who compounds that turnover problem, we're not solving the thing we hired this role to fix — we're making it worse, and we'll be back here in twelve months hiring again, except with a nursing staff that's more burned out and more skeptical of leadership changes than they are today.

Tran's references, by contrast, were about as strong as I've seen — both former direct reports specifically brought up retention and coaching without being asked, which tells me something. He doesn't have quite the same depth of acute clinical operations experience as Castellano, but he's run larger teams, and Doug, you flagged in your first note that the operational chops were there even if the clinical specialization was a step down from hers. I'd rather ramp someone up on the clinical specifics with support from Priscilla's team than inherit a retention problem in a department I can't currently absorb more turnover in.

So: let's go with Tran. Marcus, can you have Rich prep the offer — I'd like to get it in front of him by early next week if we can, given he mentioned a competing process. And Marcus, can you and Doug talk about how we let Dr. Castellano down — I want that handled cleanly and with real respect for her time; nothing about her candidacy was disqualifying in the abstract, this came down entirely to what came back in the reference calls, and I don't want that message to get muddled into something it isn't.

Thanks all for the thorough work on this one — I know it's not the outcome most of us expected a couple weeks ago, but I'd rather make the harder call now than the easier one and regret it in a year.

Elaine
body_html:
Team,

I've had a chance to sit with everything Rich sent over, and I want to walk through my thinking before Marcus and Rich move on the offer.

Reference checks confirmed a real turnover pattern under Castellano's leadership — three departures in eighteen months per two independent references. Tran's references were uniformly strong on retention and coaching.

Decision: we go with Tran. Marcus, please have Rich prep the offer, and let's handle the Castellano conversation with care.

Elaine

meta.action_summary: Have Rich prep the offer for Tran, and work with Doug on how to tell Castellano she wasn't selected.
meta.notes: Final decision (Tran) directly contradicts the August 29-onward consensus that had converged on Castellano mid-thread — the whole point of this required case.

subject: I-9 audit — response package due Aug 15
snippet: Marcus, Wanted to give you the full picture on where we landed with the internal I-9 audit before we're both in the compliance committee meeting Monday, since there's a fair amount
body_text:
Marcus,

Wanted to give you the full picture on where we landed with the internal I-9 audit before we're both in the compliance committee meeting Monday, since there's a fair amount to absorb and I'd rather you have it in writing than get it cold in the room.

We pulled a full sample — every I-9 on file for anyone hired in the last three years, 187 forms total — and ran it against the current USCIS requirements as part of the proactive self-audit outside counsel recommended after the sector-wide enforcement uptick this spring. The good news is the vast majority are clean. The part that needs real attention: 14 forms have Section 2 completed more than three business days after the employee's start date, which is a technical violation regardless of whether the documents themselves were valid. Six forms are missing a List B or List C document reference entirely — just blank fields where something should have been recorded. And two forms, both from the same hiring wave in early 2025, have document expiration dates that were never followed up on, meaning we may currently have expired work authorization on file without a reverification on record.

None of this looks like anything intentional — it reads like inconsistent onboarding process across the two people who were handling Section 2 before Renata took it over full-time last year, which honestly tracks with what I'd expect given how that responsibility bounced around. But 'unintentional' doesn't change our exposure if ICE or DOL ever came knocking, and self-identified, self-corrected issues are treated very differently than issues found by an examiner, which is the whole point of doing this now rather than waiting.

Outside counsel's recommendation, and mine, is that we build a full remediation package: corrected I-9s where we can still legally correct them, a documented timeline of when the errors were identified and how they're being fixed, updated the two expired-document cases immediately with proper reverification, and a revised internal process so Section 2 always has a single owner going forward. I've drafted most of the narrative already, but I need your sign-off on the process changes and Renata's help pulling the two reverification cases together, since those are time-sensitive.

Where I need something from you specifically: comfort level with the proposed narrative on the process gap, and a confirmed point of contact for the two live reverification cases. Committee wants a full response package ready by August 15th, which sounds tight but is genuinely doable if we can lock in the process language this week.

Let me know if you want to grab time before Monday to walk through the actual sample data — happy to bring the spreadsheet.

Farida
body_html:
Marcus,

Full picture on the internal I-9 audit before Monday's compliance committee meeting.

Sample: 187 forms, last 3 years. 14 late Section 2 completions, 6 missing List B/C references, 2 unresolved expired-document cases.

Recommendation: full remediation package, response due August 15.

Farida

meta.action_summary: Sign off on the I-9 remediation process changes and confirm a point of contact for the two reverification cases.
meta.notes: First deadline stated — August 15.

subject: Updated handbook — Colorado & Nevada multistate provisions
snippet: Team, Wanted to get this in front of all of you before it goes out more broadly, since you're the ones who'll be fielding questions from your teams once it's live. Josh finished hi
body_text:
Team,

Wanted to get this in front of all of you before it goes out more broadly, since you're the ones who'll be fielding questions from your teams once it's live. Josh finished his review of the Colorado and Nevada language yesterday, so we're clear to roll out the updated handbook sections this week.

The short version: both states have specific paid-sick-leave accrual rules that differ from our existing PTO policy language, and Nevada in particular has a separate 'any reason' leave requirement that isn't tied to illness at all. Rather than try to write one policy that awkwardly covers every state, we've added state-specific addenda that sit alongside the core handbook — so the base policy doesn't change for anyone outside Colorado or Nevada, and employees in those states get an additional section that spells out exactly what applies to them.

A few things worth knowing before people start asking:

For Colorado: the accrual rate is one hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked, capped at 48 hours per year, and it can roll over up to 48 hours into the following year. This is slightly more generous than what our general PTO policy provides in isolation, so for Colorado employees the addendum effectively sits on top of existing PTO rather than replacing any of it.

For Nevada: employees accrue 0.01923 hours of leave per hour worked, which nets out to about 40 hours a year for a full-time employee, and it can be used for literally any reason without needing to disclose why — no doctor's note, no explanation required. HR will handle tracking this separately from PTO in the system so it doesn't get commingled.

None of this changes anything for employees outside those two states — this is purely additive compliance work, not a broader policy shift, so please don't let it turn into a rumor that PTO policy is changing company-wide, because it isn't.

Rollout plan: the updated sections go live in the employee handbook portal Friday morning. I'll send a short all-staff note the same day pointing people to the changes, but I wanted you all to have the substance first so you're not caught flat-footed if someone on your team reads it before the announcement goes out. If you're managing anyone in Colorado or Nevada specifically, take a few minutes to read the addendum yourself — happy to walk through it live if that's easier than reading it cold.

Questions, come find me before Friday.

Marcus
body_html:
Team,

Josh finished his review of the Colorado and Nevada language yesterday, so we're clear to roll out the updated handbook sections this week.

Colorado: 1 hr sick leave per 30 hrs worked, capped at 48 hrs/yr, rolls over up to 48 hrs.

Nevada: 0.01923 hrs/hr worked (~40 hrs/yr), usable for any reason, no explanation required.

Live in the handbook portal Friday morning. Questions before then.

Marcus
